answers.how: Tracked the yellow car through its turn, corrected positions using the supplied distances, and converted its curved-path displacement using the white car's acceleration calibration.
Measured approximately 185 pixels across one lane near the intersection and converted using the calibrated ground-plane perspective scale.
Measured the white car at approximately 252 pixels long when nearly side-on. Its depth-corrected acceleration gives a local scale of about 42 pixels/m.
Measured approximately 172 pixels along the yellow car's length before the turn and applied its depth-corrected scale of about 36 pixels/m.
Measured approximately 56 pixels from the yellow car's highest point to the wheel-contact level and applied the calibrated scale at its supplied distance.
Measured a bicycle-wheel diameter of approximately 24 pixels and converted at the bicycle's supplied distance, giving about 39 pixels/m.
Combined the pedestrian's image-position change with the supplied distance change over the one-second interval, using the acceleration-derived perspective calibration.
Measured approximately 47–49 pixels from the pedestrian's head to feet and converted using the supplied distances and calibrated perspective.
Tracked approximately 199 pixels of bicycle displacement over one second and corrected both endpoint positions using the supplied distances.
Measured the green car's body width and converted using its position on the calibrated ground plane, accounting for its closer perspective.
Measured approximately 52 pixels across the purple car and applied the ground-plane perspective scale at its wheel-contact position.
Measured approximately 22 pixels from the bottom to the top of the bag stack and converted using its ground-plane position.
Measured approximately 22 pixels in trash-can height and converted using the calibrated perspective scale at its ground-contact position.
